terms.definition: Tape Archive — a Linux command-line tool that bundles multiple files and directories into a single archive file without compression. Extension: .tar
terms.example: Like putting multiple clothes into one suitcase without vacuum-sealing it.

terms.definition: GNU Zip — a Linux compression tool that reduces the size of a single file. Used after TAR to compress archives. Extension adds .gz
terms.example: Like vacuum-sealing the suitcase after packing to make it smaller.

terms.definition: A tool that performs both archiving (bundling) and compression in a single step. Cross-platform compatible. Required for AWS Lambda deployments.
terms.example: Like a smart bag that automatically packs and compresses everything at once.

terms.definition: A single file that bundles multiple files and directories together. Created by TAR. Does not reduce size on its own.
terms.example: A single .tar file containing 100 individual files.

terms.definition: The process of reducing the size of a file using algorithms that eliminate redundant data. Reduces storage and transfer costs.
terms.example: A 10MB .tar file compressed to 3MB .tar.gz.

terms.definition: Virtual Private Cloud — a logically isolated virtual network within AWS where you launch and manage your cloud resources. Scoped to one AWS Region.
terms.example: Like the boundary wall of a school campus — defining your private, isolated territory.

terms.definition: A subdivision of a VPC's IP address range. Always tied to a single Availability Zone. Can be public (internet-accessible) or private (internal only).
terms.example: Like individual zones (Zone 1, Zone 2) within the school campus, each serving different purposes.

terms.definition: An AWS VPC component that enables communication between your VPC and the public internet. One IGW per VPC. Horizontally scalable and highly available by default.
terms.example: The main gate of the school — the only official entry/exit point for outsiders.

terms.definition: A set of rules (routes) that determine where network traffic within a VPC is directed. Each subnet is associated with one route table.
terms.example: Signboards at each zone entrance telling people (traffic packets) which direction to go.

terms.definition: Network Access Control List — a stateless subnet-level firewall in AWS. Evaluates inbound and outbound rules in number order. Supports both ALLOW and DENY rules.
terms.example: The zone-level security guard (S1) who checks everyone entering and leaving the zone.

terms.definition: A stateful resource-level firewall in AWS. Controls inbound and outbound traffic for individual instances or services. Supports ALLOW rules only.
terms.example: The department-level security guard (S2) at each room door who checks credentials per room.

terms.definition: A firewall behaviour where each packet is evaluated independently, with no memory of previous connections. Return traffic must be explicitly allowed. NACLs are stateless.
terms.example: A guard who checks your ID every single time you enter AND leave, with no memory of past visits.

terms.definition: A firewall behaviour where connection state is tracked. If inbound traffic is allowed, return traffic is automatically permitted. Security Groups are stateful.
terms.example: A guard who stamps your hand when you enter and automatically lets you out without checking again.

terms.definition: Classless Inter-Domain Routing — a method of specifying IP address ranges using a base IP and a prefix length (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16). Defines the IP address space of a VPC or subnet.
terms.example: 10.0.0.0/16 means the VPC can use IP addresses from 10.0.0.0 to 10.0.255.255 (65,536 addresses).

terms.definition: A subnet whose route table has a route directing internet-bound traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to an Internet Gateway. Resources here can be reached from the internet if they have public IPs.
terms.example: Zone 1 in the school — the playground and admin area accessible to authorised outsiders.

terms.definition: A subnet whose route table has NO route to an Internet Gateway. Resources here cannot be directly accessed from the internet. Used for databases and backend services.
terms.example: Zone 2 in the school — labs and classrooms accessible only to internal school staff and students.

terms.definition: Temporary ports (range 1024–65535) used by clients for the return half of a TCP connection. NACLs must allow these ports outbound for web traffic to work correctly.
terms.example: When your browser requests port 80, the server responds back to a randomly assigned ephemeral port on your machine.

terms.definition: The verbose flag in TAR commands. When included, TAR prints the name of each file as it is archived or extracted. Useful for monitoring progress.
terms.example: Adding -v to tar -cvf shows each filename as it is added: file1.txt, file2.txt, sample/...

terms.definition: The command used to decompress a .gz file. The opposite of gzip. Removes the .gz extension and restores the original file.
terms.example: gunzip myarchive.tar.gz restores myarchive.tar.

terms.definition: An AWS-provided VPC automatically created in each region for every new AWS account. Comes pre-configured with subnets, IGW, and route tables so you can launch instances immediately.
terms.example: Like a furnished apartment — ready to move in without any setup, but you can customise it later.
